record_notes.DCP-LETT-1757: Day 29 with September 1855 supplied from recent Huxley marriage and autumn reference; later than September 3 source 1759 despite lower ID. Missing Huxley anatomical letter provoked detailed response, not a surviving Darwin outgoing substituted as prompt. Darwin admits weak microscopy, distinguishes observed ducts and cellular appearances from interpretation as true ovaria, defends repeated connections while accepting that gut-formed gland relation may differ. Own failure to see cement gland in Lepas remains explicit, contrasted with other genera. Leonard artist drawing recalled is not itself reproduced here. Footnote 3 loosely associates gut-formed gland with cement gland, while body explicitly refuses that identity; retain source-layer distinction. P1 includes see P.S. cross-reference. In P7 he newly retrieves, examines and breaks up preserved specimen, finding pulpy matter and no cell with included nuclei/granules in that specimen, while maintaining he saw cells in others. Do not flatten this later examination into pre-existing observation in P1–6 or global retraction of all observations. Later Huxley 1857 lecture, Krohn 1859 criticism and modern Crisp analysis remain apparatus, not a preserved incoming prompt or Darwin present knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1668: Explicit accepted primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. April 18 with supplied 1855 year. Forwards missing Bell opinion, asks recipient to read and burn: historical quoted instruction does not authorize any file deletion. Acknowledges Lindley higher claim but uncertain about alternating biological subfields; weighs Hancock/Westwood and quotes Huxley opinion to Bell. Has written Bell but meeting and final award decisions still future. Huxley note on Lyell separate missing input. Reports De la Beche death. Later rule history and medal outcomes are editorial evidence, not assumptions about current settled procedure.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1697: Explicit accepted primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Explicit accepted batch-15 primary full reading reused with matching source pins. June 10 with supplied 1855 year. Independently read additional witness in full. Asks Huxley to speak for Barrande and Dana at next council if Darwin cannot attend, explicitly enclosing an old Lyell note; footnote identifies April 23 source 1672 and shared dual candidature plus Barrande primordial work confirms it. Conditional request not to answer if attending does not prove attendance. Huxley lecture abstract has been read with disappointment; exact title identity is apparatus and missing cover note remains missing. Upcoming marriage congratulations are not proof wedding already occurred. Later June 14 and July 21 events separate. This source is not a reply to Lyell but uses his incoming evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1759: Explicit accepted primary full reading reused with matching source and acceptance pins. Day 3 with September 1855 supplied from related drawing chronology. Huxley drawings received and annotated; no separate surviving cover-note text. Actual two preserved images viewed: stalked Lepas anatomy with cement-gland arrow, ovarian branching, oesophagus/stomach and peduncle-muscle directions; sessile Balanus drawing with pencil cross and sub-oesophageal-ganglion placement direction. These combine Huxley imagery and Darwin corrections; cannot use amended image as pristine incoming prompt or turn editorially typeset image captions into invented original prose. Body distinguishes unseen Lepas cement gland from probable position by analogy, and asks ganglion, stomach, antenna and testes changes. No proof original physical ink/pencil layers can be isolated from these reproductions. Later printed revised drawings in 1857 remain future.

Source reproduction mixes drawing, marks and editorially typeset annotation, not pure incoming diagram.
